Es sei \(L(s)\) die für \(\text{Re}(s)>0\) durch \(\sum^ \infty_{j=0}(- 1)^ j(2j+1)^{-s}\) definierte Dirichletsche \(L\)-Funktion. Die Verf. beweisen zahlreiche Reihen- und Integraldarstellungen von \(L(g)\) bei natürlichem \(g\), die in analoger Form auch für \(\zeta(g+1)\) gelten. Von besonderer Bedeutung sind dabei die schnell konvergenten Reihendarstellungen von \(L(g)\), deren Definition auf den Koeffizienten \(t(j,k)\) der Taylorentwicklung 
\[
\left(2\;\text{arcsinh} \qquad{x\over 2}\right)^ k=k!\sum^ \infty_{j=k}t(j,k){x^ j\over j!} (| x|<2;\;k=0,1,2,\dots)
\]
 beruht. Für ganzes \(m\geq 0\), \(r=0,1\) mit \(2m+r\geq 1\) ergibt sich 
\[
\begin{multlined}2^{2m+r}L(2m+r)=\sum^{m+r- 1}_{k=0}\sum^ \infty_{j=k}{(-1)^ jt(2j+1,2k+1)\over (2j)! (j+1/2)^{2m-2k+r}}+\\ +\sum^ \infty_{n=m+r-1}h_{r,n}{(- 1)^{n+1}t(2n+1,2m-(-1)^ r )\over (2n+1)!}\end{multlined}
\]
 mit \(h_{1,n}={1\over 2}\), \(h_{0,n}=2^{2n+1}\left(\log 2- \sum_{j=1}^{2n+1}{2^{-j}\over j}\right)\) und damit insbesondere 
\[
L(1)={\pi\over 4}={3\over 4}\sum^ \infty_{j=0}{2j\choose j}{2^{- 4j}\over 2j+1}.
\]

editorial_contributions.text:
For \(a,b,c\not\in\{0,-1,-2,\ldots\}\) and \(|z|<1\) the Gauss hypergeometric function \( _2F_1(a,b,c;z)\) is defined by 
\[ _2F_1(a,b,c;z)=1+\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{(a)_k(b)_k}{(c)_k} \cdot\frac{z^k}{k!},\] 
where \((x)_k=x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)\). In the paper, the authors  prove that for \(n\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\) and \(0<|z|<1\),
\[
 _2F_1\Big(n+\frac 12,n+\frac 12,n+\frac 32;-z^2\Big)
=\frac{2n+1}{z^{2n}} \Big(\frac{\operatorname{arcsinh} z}{z}-\frac 1{(1+z^2)^{\frac{2n-1}2}} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\frac{z^{2j}(1+z^2)^{n-1-j}}{2j+1}\Big)
\]
and 
\[ _2F_1\Big(1,n+\frac 12,n+\frac 32;z^2\Big)=\frac{2n+1}{z^{2n}} \Big(\frac{\operatorname{arctanh} z}{z}-\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{z^{2k}}{2k+1}\Big).\] 
It is easy to see that
\[
\frac{z^{2n}}{2n+1}\; _2F_1\Big(1,n+\frac 12,n+\frac 32;z^2\Big)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{z^{2n+2k}}{2n+2k+1} \]
\[
=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{2k}}{2k+1} -\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{z^{2k}}{2k+1}=\frac{\operatorname{arctanh} z}z-\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{z^{2k}}{2k+1}.
\]
Thus, the authors' result for \( _2F_1(1,n+\frac 12,n+\frac 32;z^2)\) is quite clear.

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(\zeta\) denote the Riemann zeta function. The aim of the paper under review  is to show the following integral evaluations
\begin{align*}
\int_0^1 \frac{\arcsin x \arccos x}{x} \, dx &= \frac{7}{8} \zeta(3), \\
\frac{2}{\pi} \int_0^1 \frac{\arcsin^2 x \arccos x}{x} \, dx &= \frac{1}{8} \zeta(3),
\end{align*}
and discuss their applications to central binomial series, multiple zeta values, and some other sums shown as Theorems 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.11, 2.16, 2.23. The main idea is to evaluate integrals involving powers of arcsine function.

Theorem 2.6.
Let \(G\) denote the Catalan constant
\[
G = 1 - \frac{1}{3^2} + \frac{1}{5^2} - \frac{1}{7^2} + \cdots \approx 0.915966 \dots
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
\int_0^1 \frac{\mathrm{arcsinh} \, x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}} \, dx &= G, \\
\int_0^1 \frac{\mathrm{arcsinh} \, x\arccos x}{x} \, dx &= \frac{\pi^3}{32}.
\end{align*}

Theorem 2.7.
\[
\int_0^1 \frac{\arctan x \operatorname{arcctg} x}{x} \, dx = \frac{7}{8} \zeta(3).
\]

For positive integers \(i_1, \dots, i_k\) such that \(i_1 \geq 2\), define the multiple zeta value and multiple \(t\)-value by
\begin{align*}
\zeta(i_1, i_2, \dots, i_k) &= \sum_{n_1 > n_2 > \cdots > n_k > 0} \frac{1}{n_1^{i_1} n_2^{i_2} \cdots n_k^{i_k}}, \\
t(i_1, i_2, \dots, i_k) &= \sum_{\substack{n_1 > n_2 > \cdots > n_k > 0 \\ n_j \text{ odd}}} \frac{1}{n_1^{i_1} n_2^{i_2} \cdots n_k^{i_k}}.
\end{align*}
Let \(\{m\}^n\) denote the sequence \((m, m, \dots, m)\) of length \(n\).

Theorem 2.16.
For \(n \geq 0\),
\begin{align*}
\zeta(3, \{2\}^n) &= \frac{2}{\pi} \int_0^1 \frac{2^{2n+3}\arcsin^{2n+2} x \arccos x}{ (2n+2)! x} \, dx, \\
t(3, \{2\}^n) &= \int_0^1 \frac{\arcsin^{2n+1} x \arccos x}{(2n+1)! x} \, dx.
\end{align*}

The author finishes the article with the following  conjecture.

Conjecture 2.26.
\[
\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{\binom{2k}{k}}{2^{2k} (2k+1)^4} = \frac{1}{48} \left( 6\pi \zeta(3) + 4\pi \log^3 2 + \pi^3 \log 2 \right).
\]

Recently, quite similar series  were  evaluated by \textit{J. Ablinger} in [Exp. Math. 26, No. 1, 62--71 (2017; Zbl 1365.05009)] by method of iterated integrals, integration by parts, and generating functions.The author expects that the  conjecture can be proved with some similar idea.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Using two Jacobi elliptic equations as auxiliary equations, the generalized sinh-Gordon equation is studied in this paper. With the aid of mathematical software Maple, many new interaction exact solutions of the generalized sinh-Gordon equation are obtained. These solutions involve combinations of the arcsinh function, Jacobi elliptic functions, hyperbolic functions and trigonometric functions.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Let \(p\in\mathbb{R}\), \(M\) be a bivariate mean, and \(M_p\) be defined by \(M_p(a, b) = M^{1/p}( a^p, b^p)\) (\(p\neq 0\)) and \(M_0( a, b) = \lim_{p\to 0} M_p( a, b)\). In this paper, we prove that the sharp inequalities \(L_2(a, b) < P(a, b) < NS_{1/2}(a, b)< He(a, b)< A_{2/3}(a, b)< I(a, b)< Z_{1/3}(a, b)< Y_{1/2}(a, b)\) hold for all \(a,b > 0\) with \(a \neq b\), where \(L(a, b) =(a-b)/(\log a - \log b)\), \(P(a, b)=(a-b)/[2\arcsin((a-b)/(a+b))]\), \(NS(a, b)=(a-b)/[2\operatorname{arcsinh}((a-b)/(a+b))]\), \(He(a, b)= (a+ \sqrt{ab}+ b)/3\), \(A(a, b)=(a+b)/2\), \(I(a, b)=1/ e(a^a/ b^b)^{1/( a - b)}\), \(Z( a, b) = a^{a/(a+ b)} b^{b/(a+b)}\) and \(Y (a, b) = I(a, b)e^{1- ab/L^2(a, b)}\) are respectively the logarithmic, first Seiffert, Neuman-Sándor, Heronian, arithmetic, identric, power-exponential and exponential-geometric means of \(a\) and \(b\).

editorial_contributions.text:
In this paper, the authors study the properties of Meixner-Pollaczek polynomials by applying the central difference operator to solve the corresponding Sturm-Liouville problem. The Meixner-Pollaczek polynomials are defined by
\[
P_n^\lambda(x,\phi)=e^{in\phi}\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(\lambda+ix)_k(\lambda-ix)_{n-k}}{k!(n-k)!}e^{-2ik\phi},
\]
for \(0<\phi<\pi\), \(\lambda>0\) and \(x\in\mathbb{R}\), where \((\alpha)_k\) is the Pochhammer symbol.

The central difference operator \(T\) is defined by
\[
T(f)(x)=\frac{f(x+i/2)-f(x-i/2)}{i}.
\]
In general, \(T^k[P_n^\lambda(x,\phi)]=(2\sin\phi)^kP_{n-k}^{\lambda+k/2}(x,\phi)\) if \(k\leq n\).

In this context, the exponential function \(E^\lambda(x,t)\) is defined by
\[
E^\lambda(x,t)=g_\lambda(t)\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(\lambda+(1-n)/2+ix)_n}{n!}t^n,
\]
where \(g_\lambda(t)\) is a constant, such that, \(E^\lambda(0,t)=1\). In particular, \(T E^\lambda(x,t)=itE^\lambda(x,t)\). Then, the following expansion is obtained
\[
E(x,t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \left( \frac{it}{2\text{sin}\phi}\right)^n \left( \frac{\text{sin}\phi}{2\text{sin}(\phi+i\text{arcsinh}(t/2))}\right)^{2\lambda+n}P_n^\lambda(x,\phi).
\]
The operator \(T\) is densely defined on the space \(L_2(\mathbb{R},dx)\). 

The following result is proved.

Theorem 1. Let \(f\) and \(g\) be analytic in the strip \(-1\leq \Im z\leq 1\) and
\[
\lim_{x\to \pm \infty}\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|f(x+iy+iu)|^2dy=\lim_{x\to \pm \infty}\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|g(x+iy+iu)|^2dy=0
\]
uniformly for \(|u|\leq 1/2\). Assume that \(f\) and \(g\) are real-valued on \(\mathbb{R}\). Then there holds: \(T^*=-T\).

Now, consider the analogue of the Sturm-Liouville equation:
\[
\frac{1}{w(x)}T(p(x)Ty_n(x))=\lambda_ny_n(x).
\]

The authors obtain the next theorem.

Theorem 2. Assuming that \(p(x)\) is positive definite, the operator \(\frac{1}{w(x)}T[(p(x)T]\) is a positive operator on the space \(L_2(\mathbb{R},dx)\), and satisfies the assumptions of Theorem 1.

Using the recurrence relation for Meixner-Pollaczek polynomials and Darboux' asymptotic method, the following explicit representation is derived:
\[
P^*_n(x,\lambda,\phi)=2\sin \phi\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{P_k^\lambda(x,\phi)P_{n-k-1}^{1-\lambda}(-x,\phi)}{n-k}.
\]

Finally, the authors introduce a suitable function  \(Q_n^\lambda(z,\phi)\) such that \(TQ_n^\lambda(z,\phi)=2\sin\phi \, Q_{n-1}^{\lambda+1/2}(z,\phi)\) and
\[
T[w(z,\lambda,\phi)Q_n^\lambda(z,\phi)]=-(n+1)w(z,\lambda-1/2,\phi)Q_{n+1}^{\lambda-1/2}(z,\phi).
\]
